exclusion_criteria.value: Patients were excluded from the study for the following reasons: a) an existing contraindication for placing an esophageal balloon; b) the patient required continuous paralysis or heavy sedation; c) the patient was comatose or had a progressive neurologic injury; d) the patient had a chest tube in place that might interfere with some of the necessary measurements; and e) the patient was receiving peritoneal dialysis or had acquired immunodeficiency syndrome.

outcomes.name_verbatim: Duration of mechanical ventilation after study entry

provenance.quote: The mean duration of mechanical ventilation after study entry was 5.33 +/- 2.5 days.
If the clinician had noted the ``twinkle in the patient's eye'' on all occasions, the duration on mechanical ventilation would have been 7.02 +/- 2.66 days after entry into the study.

Comparing this latter result to the actual duration of mechanical ventilation using the Student's paired t-test shows that the esophageal weaning protocol shortened ventilatory stay by 1.68 days when compared with the clinical weaning protocol (p < .05).

outcomes.name_verbatim: Calculated duration of mechanical ventilation if weaned solely by clinical evaluation

provenance.quote: Had the patient been weaned solely by the clinical evaluation, the duration of mechanical ventilation would have been 7.81 +/- 2.8 days.

outcomes.name_verbatim: Comparison of esophageal and clinical weaning protocols

paired_effects.contrast: Esophageal weaning protocol more aggressive than clinical weaning protocol (40.5% vs 11.6% of 138 decisions)

provenance.quote: McNemar's statistic for comparing dichotomous outcomes demonstrated that the esophageal weaning protocol was more aggressive than the clinical weaning protocol (p < .001)
In five instances in the clinical protocol and in six instances in the esophageal protocol, the patient did not tolerate the predicted number of weaning steps.

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: Study used esophageal balloon to guide weaning, not PEEP titration; no transpulmonary pressure target. Timing from intubation not reported; patients had been ventilated for at least 3 days before study entry.

unclear_items: adults_18_plus: No explicit age criterion stated; assumed adult ICU.
balloon_calibration.method: Position verified 'in the usual manner' but no specific calibration method reported.
timing_subgroup: Reference event unclear; patients had MV for at least 3 days before study entry but exact time from intubation not reported.
Outcome data: Clinical weaning duration of 7.81 days (without acceleration) and 7.02 days (with acceleration) both reported; used 7.02 for paired comparison and 7.81 as separate calculated outcome.
extraction_flags.general_notes: Study excluded from review because esophageal balloon data guided weaning, not PEEP titration.
